question.text: In alpha-beta separation, a portfolio manager wants to isolate alpha from market beta. Which of the following combinations achieves this?

answer.text: Long active portfolio + Short market-neutral index
Long active portfolio + Short broad-market index/futures
Long passive ETF + Short active portfolio
Long active portfolio + Long broad-market index

explanation.text: The Logic: To strip market beta from an active portfolio, go long the active portfolio and short the broad-market index (via futures or ETFs). The residual is alpha. Beta can then be overlaid separately via a passive index exposure. The Trap: Option A (short market-neutral) makes no sense — market-neutral has zero beta. The correct hedge uses a long-beta instrument (market index/futures). Cross-Exam Context: VIII (Equity Derivatives) covers index-futures hedging math; XXI-B combines with portable-alpha concept. Manager's Pro-Tip: Portable alpha = take alpha from one asset class and transport beta from another — popular with institutional pension funds globally, less common in Indian PMS.
